title: Stop being whirled around
hookLine: don't let outside things distract you; make time to learn something good (Meditations 2.7)

cards: Eleven browser tabs. A half-written email. A notification, then another.
You check the news, then the weather, then the news again, in case it changed in the last four minutes. A day like that can leave a person worn out by evening, with nothing finished to show for it.
Book two has a word for that state, and it's a physical one: whirled around. Spun, like a top, or a leaf in a gust of wind.

teach.b: First, the question. Section seven opens: do the things outside you distract you? Marcus was running an empire at war.
If anyone had a reason to be distracted, it was him. Second, the cure.
In Long's translation: "Give thyself time to learn something new and good, and cease to be whirled around." The cure isn't, empty your mind. It's, give yourself something good to learn.
A mind with nothing to hold onto spins. A mind with something worth learning has a center. Third, the second mistake.

Then Marcus catches himself, because there's a trap on the other side. Some people, he says, wear themselves out with activity, and yet have no aim to which they direct every movement and every thought.

teach.h: BUSY, BUT AIMLESS, IS SPINNING TOO.
teach.b: Busy, but still spinning. Being whirled around by outside things is one mistake; whirling yourself around with aimless busyness is the other. Both look like motion.
Neither goes anywhere. Fourth, the aim.
What Marcus wants is a center: one aim that every movement points toward. Here he doesn't say what his own aim was. It doesn't have to be grand.
A good day, a kind word, a piece of work done well.
The spinning slows when there's something in the middle. Not all motion has to stop. Just one spinning thing, one tab, one loop of checking, and in the time you get back, one good thing learned.

how: Readers who take this entry to heart often set a single aim for the day and cut one habitual distraction, using the time to study something worthwhile.

games.q: what does “stop being whirled around” mean?
o: sit perfectly still until every thought has stopped

games.q: your day is a blur of checking and switching. you decide to fix it by doubling your activity. what does Meditations 2.7 say?
o: careful: busy without an aim is still spinning.
give up; distraction can't be helped.
games.why: Marcus warns against both errors: being whirled around by outside things, and wearing yourself out with aimless activity.

practice: Let the day's spinning come to mind, the checking, the switching, the half-done things, and watch them circle like leaves in wind without fighting them.
Then find the center, one aim for today, simple and real, and let your breath settle around it.

wordCard.voice: Stop being whirled around. Marcus's cure for distraction: learn something new and good, and give every movement an aim, so busyness isn't just more spinning. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: stop spinning. Something good in the middle slows the whirl. That's day five hundred thirty-three.

sources.q: Give thyself time to learn something new and good, and cease to be whirled around.
